positive.scenario: A document with a non-empty title passes.

negative.scenario: The failing fixture has no usable title and reports the rule.

inapplicable.notApplicable: The page-title rule is document-scoped and is always applicable for a full-page document scan.

exception.notApplicable: The implemented WCAG 2.4.2 page-title check has no automated authoring exception.

positive.scenario: A visible image with an accessible alternative passes.

negative.scenario: An image without an accessible alternative fails.

inapplicable.scenario: Only image semantics contribute applicability; unrelated fixture content does not become an image-name candidate.

exception.scenario: Specialized image-like semantics reuse the image-name rule without manufacturing duplicate findings.

positive.scenario: A named button passes accessible-name evaluation.

negative.scenario: An unnamed button fails with accessible-name evidence.

inapplicable.scenario: Scopes without button candidates do not create button findings.

exception.scenario: An icon-only button named by its descendant SVG is accepted.

positive.scenario: A form control with a computed accessible name passes.

negative.scenario: An unnamed form control is reported by the failing fixture.

inapplicable.scenario: Non-form elements are excluded from form-control name evaluation.

exception.scenario: Placeholder fallback is not promoted to an accessible-name failure and remains a review signal.

positive.scenario: A link with discernible accessible text passes.

negative.scenario: An unnamed link is reported by the failing fixture.

inapplicable.scenario: Content without link candidates does not produce link-name findings.

exception.scenario: Ambiguous link purpose remains contextual review evidence instead of being promoted to this empty-name failure.

positive.scenario: An aria-hidden subtree without a sequentially focusable descendant does not fail.

negative.scenario: A sequentially focusable button inside aria-hidden=true produces the deterministic failure.

inapplicable.scenario: A selected scan scope with no applicable aria-hidden subtree contributes no candidate for this rule.

exception.scenario: Non-focusable content inside aria-hidden remains accepted rather than being treated as a blanket aria-hidden failure.

positive.scenario: Visible label text contained in the accessible name passes.

negative.scenario: A visible label not represented in the accessible name fails.

inapplicable.scenario: Controls without an applicable visible text label are excluded.

exception.scenario: Normalization and symbol handling cover Label in Name matching exceptions.

positive.scenario: A document with a non-empty lang value passes the presence check.

negative.scenario: A document without html lang fails.

inapplicable.notApplicable: The primary page-language presence rule is document-scoped and always applies to a full-page scan.

exception.notApplicable: The implemented presence check has no authoring exception once a document is scanned.

positive.scenario: A known primary language subtag passes.

negative.scenario: An unknown primary language subtag fails.

inapplicable.scenario: When html lang is missing, validity is left inapplicable and FT-WCAG-008 owns the failure.

exception.scenario: Known primary subtags remain accepted when later subtags are non-standard.

positive.scenario: Text meeting the required contrast ratio passes deterministic evaluation.

negative.scenario: Low text contrast produces structured deterministic evidence.

inapplicable.scenario: Inactive or non-visible text candidates are excluded only where the standard permits it.

exception.scenario: Ambiguous painted stacking is downgraded to review instead of producing a false deterministic contrast failure.

positive.scenario: Deterministically measurable UI boundaries meeting the ratio pass.

negative.scenario: Deterministically measurable low non-text contrast fails.

inapplicable.scenario: Candidates outside the supported deterministic subset are excluded.

exception.scenario: Standard exemptions and contextual boundaries remain non-fail outcomes.

positive.scenario: A rectangular target containing a 24 by 24 CSS pixel area passes the WCAG 2.2 minimum-size path.

negative.scenario: Undersized targets whose 24 CSS pixel spacing circles overlap produce REVIEW, never an unsupported deterministic FAIL.

inapplicable.scenario: Disabled controls are excluded from active pointer-target evaluation.

exception.scenario: Spacing and inline-target exceptions are exercised without weakening the 24 CSS pixel minimum.

positive.scenario: Explicit language-of-parts markup with a valid language passes.

negative.scenario: Invalid explicit language-of-parts markup fails the deterministic subset.

inapplicable.scenario: Elements without explicit language-part semantics are outside this deterministic subset.

exception.scenario: Language inheritance and excluded or non-human-language cases are handled conservatively.

positive.scenario: Named tab, tooltip and summary candidates pass.

negative.scenario: Unnamed deterministic specialized controls fail.

inapplicable.scenario: Hidden and non-semantic lookalike markup is excluded.

exception.scenario: Accessible-name sources and broken-reference handling follow the shared name calculation contract.

positive.scenario: Named meter and progressbar candidates pass.

negative.scenario: Unnamed meter or progressbar candidates fail.

inapplicable.scenario: Hidden and non-semantic range lookalikes are excluded.

exception.scenario: Native label and ARIA naming paths are both exercised.

positive.scenario: A top-level body without aria-hidden=true passes.

negative.scenario: A top-level body with aria-hidden=true fails.

inapplicable.scenario: The page-body rule does not run for a component root.

exception.scenario: aria-hidden=false is explicitly accepted and does not behave like true.

positive.scenario: A simple native data table with determinable column headers passes for its data cells.

negative.scenario: An orphan data cell in a simple table with proven header structure fails.

inapplicable.scenario: A layout-like table with no data-table evidence has zero applicability for the header-relationship rule.

exception.scenario: Unresolved complex spanning or indexed ARIA relationships are downgraded to REVIEW instead of guessed as deterministic failures.

positive.scenario: An exposed object with an aria-label or title-based accessible alternative passes.

negative.scenario: An exposed object[data] without an accessible alternative fails.

inapplicable.scenario: The rule is scoped to exposed object[data] candidates; frames and other embedded semantics are handled by their own rules.

exception.scenario: The shared accessible-name computation accepts supported ARIA and title naming paths rather than requiring one specific authoring mechanism.

positive.scenario: An exposed frame named with title or aria-label passes.

negative.scenario: An exposed unnamed frame fails the accessible-name rule.

inapplicable.scenario: Non-frame embedded content is outside frame-name applicability and is evaluated by separate rules.

exception.scenario: Duplicate frame names remain an equivalent-purpose REVIEW question rather than being converted into an automatic frame-name failure.

positive.scenario: A negative-tabindex same-origin frame passes when bounded inspection finds no sequentially focusable descendant.

negative.scenario: A negative-tabindex same-origin frame fails when its embedded document contains a sequentially focusable descendant.

inapplicable.scenario: Frames without a negative tabindex are outside this ACT-bounded sequential-focus check.

exception.scenario: Cross-origin, sandboxed or unavailable descendants become explicit coverage REVIEW evidence instead of a guessed FT-WCAG-020 failure.

positive.scenario: Viewport directives that permit at least 200 percent zoom pass the ACT-bounded check.

negative.scenario: user-scalable=no or maximum-scale below two fails the 200 percent zoom expectation.

inapplicable.scenario: Viewport metadata without user-scalable or maximum-scale restrictions contributes no applicable evaluation.

exception.scenario: Negative maximum-scale values are discarded conservatively, while finite ceilings from two to below five remain a separate larger-zoom REVIEW.

positive.scenario: A zero-delay redirect or a refresh delay beyond twenty hours passes the bounded timing expectation.

negative.scenario: A parseable delayed meta refresh inside the WCAG timing window fails.

inapplicable.scenario: Unparseable refresh metadata is ignored and does not become a deterministic timing candidate.

exception.scenario: Zero-delay redirects and delays beyond the bounded twenty-hour window are explicit pass paths rather than short time-limit failures.
